name: My Bloody Valentine
desc: The genre's center of gravity. Kevin Shields' guitar manipulations on Loveless became the template for everything after.

name: Slowdive
desc: The most emotionally resonant of the originals — ethereal, melancholy, patient.

name: Ride
desc: Oxford four-piece whose Nowhere is a foundational text — propulsive, melodic, kinetic.

name: Cocteau Twins
desc: Liz Fraser's glossolalia and Robin Guthrie's effects-drenched guitars laid the entire blueprint.

name: The Jesus and Mary Chain
desc: Psychocandy invented the feedback-pop hybrid that shoegaze would refine.

name: Lush
desc: Sharper, more pop-forward songwriting than most of their scene peers.

name: Swervedriver
desc: The muscular, motorik, road-tripping end of the scene.

name: Hum
desc: Illinois band whose 90s records and 2020 reunion defined the heavy-melodic blueprint everyone is now copying.

name: Chapterhouse
desc: Whirlpool is criminally underrated — dance-leaning, sparkling shoegaze.

name: Catherine Wheel
desc: Heavier and more rock-leaning — guitar muscle with a gaze veneer.

name: Pale Saints
desc: Leeds band that was beautifully strange — fractured pop with a 4AD sensibility.

name: Curve
desc: Darker, more electronic and gothic than most of the scene.

name: Medicine
desc: The great American answer to MBV — noisier, brattier, more deranged.

name: Drop Nineteens
desc: Boston band whose Delaware is a cult classic — slacker-y, dreamy, deceptively heavy.

name: Mazzy Star
desc: Hope Sandoval's voice over David Roback's haunted Americana — desert dream pop.

discography.title: So Tonight That I Might See

name: Mojave 3
desc: Slowdive members going pastoral after the gaze imploded.

name: Spacemen 3
desc: Drugs, drone, repetition — the spiritual ancestor of shoegaze's hypnotic side.

name: Galaxie 500
desc: Boston trio whose slow, fragile records were proto-everything-good.

name: Spiritualized
desc: Jason Pierce's post-Spacemen 3 vehicle — symphonic, addictive, ecstatic.

discography.title: Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space

name: M83
desc: Anthony Gonzalez's early albums were pure cathedral-of-sound shoegaze.

discography.title: Dead Cities, Red Seas & Lost Ghosts

name: Asobi Seksu
desc: NYC band whose Citrus defined the 2000s revival — bilingual, sugary, propulsive.

name: A Place to Bury Strangers
desc: Marketed as the loudest band in NYC — abrasive, industrial, relentless.

name: DIIV
desc: The flagship indie-gaze band of the 2010s, evolving toward heavier post-shoegaze.

name: Beach House
desc: Baltimore duo perfecting the slow-build, organ-and-guitar dream pop format.

name: Nothing
desc: Philadelphia band founded by ex-hardcore members; lush, beautiful, often harrowing.

name: Deafheaven
desc: Bay Area band whose 2013 album fused black metal blast beats with shoegaze euphoria.

name: Alcest
desc: Neige's project — foundational blackgaze, leaning more dreamy than aggressive.

name: Wisp
desc: The TikTok-era breakthrough — gauzy, intimate gaze for a new generation.

name: The Pains of Being Pure at Heart

discography.title: The Pains of Being Pure at Heart

name: Have a Nice Life
desc: Bedroom-recorded double album that became a cult phenomenon — bleak, vast, devastating.

name: Tamaryn
desc: dark gaze / dream pop — New Zealand/USA, 2010.

name: Kinoko Teikoku
desc: Tokyo band moving from heavy gaze to dreamy J-pop across their run.

name: For Tracy Hyde
desc: Bittersweet, hyper-melodic J-gaze named after a British actress.

name: Coaltar of the Deepers
desc: Genre-omnivorous Japanese project — gaze, metal, anime themes, drum 'n' bass.

name: Julie
desc: LA band channeling Nothing/Deftones heaviness with magnetic vocal interplay.

name: They Are Gutting a Body of Water
Parannoul
desc: Anonymous Korean bedroom artist whose 2021 album became an internet phenomenon.

discography.title: To See the Next Part of the Dream

name: Glare
desc: Texas band part of the current heavy-gaze revival; emotionally raw and abrasive.

discography.title: We're Not Here to Be Loved

name: This Mortal Coil
desc: Ivo Watts-Russell's 4AD supergroup of darkly beautiful covers and originals.

name: Sun's Signature
desc: Liz Fraser's long-awaited return — radiant, voice-as-instrument dream pop.

discography.title: Try Not to Destroy Everything You Love
The Things We Think We're Missing

name: Loathe
desc: Liverpool band that perfected the Deftones-meets-MBV formula on their 2020 breakthrough.
